Instruction condition is an unordered factor coded with two planned sum-to-zero contrasts:
= (−1/3, −1/3, 2/3), structure explained (C3) against not explained (C1, C2), and
= (−1/2, 1/2, 0), rules mentioned (C2) against not mentioned (C1). Planned contrasts are reported unadjusted; pairwise comparisons are Holm-adjusted.

One linear model per parameter and questionnaire, one row per participant. The outcome is the posterior mean of the parameter, standardised within the sample, so that slopes are in parameter SDs per questionnaire SD; the means and SDs are in the table below. The condition × questionnaire model (
) tests the slope averaged over the three conditions (

) estimates the slope pooled over participants. For each tested term, the Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied across the five questionnaires, separately per parameter and sample; q-values below .05 are printed in bold. Two sensitivity analyses accompany every test of a questionnaire term: the same test with a heteroscedasticity-consistent covariance (HC3), and the slope pooled over posterior draws (plausible values, Rubin’s rules), which carries the uncertainty of each participant’s estimate.
